import java.io.*;
import java.util.*;

public class Codeforces {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        BufferedReader br = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in));
        String[] parts = br.readLine().split(" ");
        int n = Integer.parseInt(parts[0]);
        double threshold = Double.parseDouble(parts[1]);

        int result = n;
        for (int x = 1; x <= n; x++) {
            if (computeProbability(n, x) >= threshold) {
                result = x;
                break;
            }
        }
        System.out.println(result);
    }

    static int nCr(int n, int r) {
        if (r > n || r < 0) return 0;
        if (r == 0 || r == n) return 1;
        r = Math.min(r, n - r);
        long res = 1;
        for (int i = 0; i < r; i++) {
            res = res * (n - i) / (i + 1);
        }
        return (int) res;
    }

    static double computeProbability(int n, int x) {
        int total = nCr(n, 3);
        
        // Case 1: All 3 maps are studied (x maps studied, 3 selected from x)
        // Both players will discard one of the studied maps, but since all are studied,
        // at least one studied map remains (3 maps - 2 discards = 1 map left)
        // The system randomly selects from remaining maps that weren't picked by any player
        // If both players discard different maps, 1 map remains; if they discard the same, 2 maps remain
        // But since opponents pick randomly, we need to compute probability carefully
        
        // Actually, let's reconsider the problem:
        // - System selects 3 maps
        // - Each player picks one map to discard (randomly if they don't know Johnny's preferences)
        // - System randomly selects one of the maps that were NOT picked by any player
        
        // For Johnny to play on a studied map:
        // We need to count cases where at least one studied map survives the discards
        
        // Let's break down by how many studied maps are in the initial 3:
        double prob = 0.0;
        
        // Case: 0 studied maps in the 3 selected
        // All 3 are unstudied. Johnny cannot win on a studied map in this case.
        // Probability of this case: C(n-x, 3) / C(n, 3)
        // Given this case, probability of playing studied map = 0
        
        // Case: 1 studied map in the 3 selected
        // 2 unstudied, 1 studied
        // Each player picks randomly among 3 maps to discard
        // For Johnny to play on studied map: the studied map must NOT be discarded by either player
        // Each player has 1/3 chance to discard the studied map
        // P(both discard unstudied) = (2/3) * (2/3) = 4/9
        // But if both discard the same unstudied map, then 2 maps remain (1 studied + 1 unstudied)
        // If they discard different unstudied maps, then 1 map remains (the studied one)
        // System randomly picks from remaining maps
        // P(studied map survives AND gets selected) = P(both discard unstudied) * P(studied gets picked | both discarded unstudied)
        // If both discard same unstudied: 2 maps remain, P(pick studied) = 1/2
        // If both discard different unstudied: 1 map remains, P(pick studied) = 1
        // P(both discard same unstudied) = 2 * (1/3 * 1/3) = 2/9 (player1 picks unstudied1, player2 picks unstudied1 OR player1 picks unstudied2, player2 picks unstudied2)
        // P(both discard different unstudied) = 2 * (1/3 * 1/3) = 2/9 (player1 picks unstudied1, player2 picks unstudied2 OR vice versa)
        // Wait, let me recalculate:
        // Player1 has 3 choices, Player2 has 3 choices = 9 total outcomes
        // Both discard same unstudied: 2 outcomes (both discard map1, both discard map2)
        // Both discard different unstudied: 2 outcomes (P1:map1,P2:map2; P1:map2,P2:map1)
        // At least one discards studied: 5 outcomes (P1:studied,P2:any; P1:not studied,P2:studied but not counted above)
        // Actually: P1 discards studied (3 outcomes for P2), P2 discards studied but P1 didn't (2 outcomes: P1 discarded map1 or map2)
        // So 3 + 2 = 5 outcomes where studied is discarded by at least one player
        // 4 outcomes where neither discards studied
        // Given neither discards studied, remaining maps = 3 - 0 = 3? No, each player discards one map, but if they discard the same map, only 1 map is discarded
        // If both discard same unstudied: 2 maps remain (1 studied + 1 unstudied), P(pick studied) = 1/2
        // If both discard different unstudied: 1 map remains (the studied one), P(pick studied) = 1
        // P(both discard same unstudied | neither discards studied) = 2/4 = 1/2
        // P(both discard different unstudied | neither discards studied) = 2/4 = 1/2
        // So P(studied map is selected | 1 studied in initial 3) = (2/9)*(1/2) + (2/9)*(1) = 1/9 + 2/9 = 3/9 = 1/3
        // Wait, let me be more systematic:
        // Total outcomes: 9
        // Neither discards studied: 4 outcomes (P1:map1,P2:map1), (P1:map1,P2:map2), (P1:map2,P2:map1), (P1:map2,P2:map2)
        // In (P1:map1,P2:map1): map1 discarded, maps {studied, map2} remain, P(pick studied) = 1/2
        // In (P1:map1,P2:map2): maps {studied} remain, P(pick studied) = 1
        // In (P1:map2,P2:map1): maps {studied} remain, P(pick studied) = 1
        // In (P1:map2,P2:map2): map2 discarded, maps {studied, map1} remain, P(pick studied) = 1/2
        // So overall: (1/2 + 1 + 1 + 1/2) / 9 = 3/9 = 1/3
        
        // Case: 2 studied maps in the 3 selected
        // 1 unstudied, 2 studied
        // Neither discards studied: both discard unstudied (only 1 such map)
        // P(both discard unstudied) = (1/3)*(1/3) = 1/9
        // If both discard unstudied: 2 studied maps remain, P(pick studied) = 1
        // If at least one discards studied: studied map might still survive
        // Let's enumerate: maps are S1, S2, U
        // Player1 choices: S1, S2, U; Player2 choices: S1, S2, U
        // Total 9 outcomes
        // Neither discards studied: only (U,U) -> 1 outcome, 2 studied remain, P=1
        // P1 discards U, P2 discards S1: remaining {S2}, P=1
        // P1 discards U, P2 discards S2: remaining {S1}, P=1
        // P1 discards S1, P2 discards U: remaining {S2}, P=1
        // P1 discards S2, P2 discards U: remaining {S1}, P=1
        // P1 discards S1, P2 discards S1: remaining {S2, U}, P=1/2
        // P1 discards S1, P2 discards S2: remaining {U}, P=0
        // P1 discards S2, P2 discards S1: remaining {U}, P=0
        // P1 discards S2, P2 discards S2: remaining {S1, U}, P=1/2
        // So P(studied selected | 2 studied in initial 3) = (1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 0 + 0 + 1/2 + 1/2) / 9 = 6/9 = 2/3
        
        // Case: 3 studied maps in the 3 selected
        // All 3 are studied
        // Neither discards studied: impossible since all are studied
        // At least one studied map always survives
        // Maps S1, S2, S3
        // P1 discards S1, P2 discards S1: remaining {S2, S3}, P=1
        // P1 discards S1, P2 discards S2: remaining {S3}, P=1
        // P1 discards S1, P2 discards S3: remaining {S2}, P=1
        // P1 discards S2, P2 discards S1: remaining {S3}, P=1
        // P1 discards S2, P2 discards S2: remaining {S1, S3}, P=1
        // P1 discards S2, P2 discards S3: remaining {S1}, P=1
        // P1 discards S3, P2 discards S1: remaining {S2}, P=1
        // P1 discards S3, P2 discards S2: remaining {S1}, P=1
        // P1 discards S3, P2 discards S3: remaining {S1, S2}, P=1
        // So P(studied selected | 3 studied in initial 3) = 1
        
        // Now compute overall probability:
        // P = P(0 studied) * 0 + P(1 studied) * (1/3) + P(2 studied) * (2/3) + P(3 studied) * 1
        
        int case0 = nCr(n - x, 3); // 0 studied maps
        int case1 = nCr(x, 1) * nCr(n - x, 2); // 1 studied, 2 unstudied
        int case2 = nCr(x, 2) * nCr(n - x, 1); // 2 studied, 1 unstudied
        int case3 = nCr(x, 3); // 3 studied maps
        
        if (total == 0) return 0.0;
        
        prob = (case1 * (1.0/3.0) + case2 * (2.0/3.0) + case3 * 1.0) / total;
        
        return prob;
    }
}
